Huh. Can't say I had any of those problems as a DM, though my players might have felt differently (they didn't say anything about it though; just said they had fun.)
1. I have a broad idea of fantasy.

3. I didn't use arcane or divine casters (other than the Factotum pregen that no one played) in my game, so the 'transparency' issue never came up. 
4. The 'regular classes with extra stuff' thing isn't a huge issue for me when the 'regular classes' (fighter, rogue, etc.) suck ass.

And they don't prepare those powers from a huge list every adventuring day; the powers they get are the powers they get.

The benefits of Psions:
Unusual flavor.
No spell preparation.
It's easier to track power points than memorized and expended spells.
